subject: Biology
title: Salmon: The Journey Home
description: A short lesson to help you apply Salmon: The Journey Home.

hook.text: Pacific salmon swim thousands of kilometers upstream to spawn in the exact stream where they were born.

buildup.text: They use Earth's magnetic field to navigate the ocean, then switch to smell to find their home stream.

discovery.text: Each river has a unique chemical signature that salmon imprint on as fry and remember for years.

twist.text: After spawning, they die. Their decaying bodies fertilize the stream, feeding the next generation.

climax.text: Bears, eagles, and forests depend on salmon runs—the fish carry ocean nutrients deep inland.

punchline.text: Born in a river. Die in the same river. Feed the next cycle.

quiz.question: How do salmon find their birth stream?
options: By smelling its unique chemical signature

details.summary: Pacific salmon hatch in freshwater streams, migrate to the ocean to grow, then navigate thousands of kilometers back to their exact birth stream to spawn and die. They use olfactory memory imprinted during youth, along with magnetic and celestial cues.
details.whyItMatters: Salmon migration connects ocean and freshwater ecosystems, transporting marine nutrients inland. Their decline from dam construction and habitat loss disrupts entire forest ecosystems that depend on salmon-derived nutrients.
takeaways: Salmon imprint on their birth stream's chemical signature as juveniles
Returning adults navigate using smell, magnetic fields, and ocean currents
Salmon carcasses deliver marine nutrients vital to forest ecosystems

faq.question: How do salmon find their exact birth stream?
faq.answer: As juveniles, salmon imprint on the unique chemical composition of their home stream. During return migration, they use magnetic navigation in the open ocean, then switch to olfactory cues as they approach rivers, literally smelling their way home.

faq.question: Why do Pacific salmon die after spawning?
faq.answer: Programmed death (semelparity) allows adults to invest all remaining energy into reproduction. Their decomposing bodies also fertilize the stream, providing nutrients that benefit their offspring. It is a final act of parental investment.
